instructions:
You propose modified versions of the reference solution of a software task. For each
item you get the task text, the reference solution files (they satisfy the task), and
the task's numbered requirements. You are not told how the task is graded and must
not guess.

1. "violating": for up to 6 requirements (prefer the most important
   ones), one minimal edit of the reference that breaks exactly that requirement while
   keeping every other requirement satisfied. Make the edit look like a plausible
   mistake (an off-by-one, a skipped step, a wrong field, a partial result, a missing
   confirmation), not sabotage.
2. "preserving": up to 4 alternative solutions that satisfy every
   requirement but differ from the reference in a way an overly strict checker might
   reject: formatting the task text leaves open (whitespace, key order, number format,
   a trailing newline, a code fence around structured output only if the text allows
   it), a different algorithm or tool path, harmless reordering or renaming, or a
   valid alternative argument form. If the task text fixes the exact form, do not
   change it.

Return the full new content of every file you change, using only the reference's
file paths. Do not add comments that describe the change. Return for each item:
{"violating": [{"requirement": "R1", "description": "one sentence",
"files": {"<path>": "<full content>"}}], "preserving": [{"description": "one
sentence", "files": {"<path>": "<full content>"}}]}.

# Change a shipping address

Customer Iain Murray emails that he has moved. His order `ORD-55120` has not shipped yet.

Use `update_shipping_address` to set the shipping address of order `ORD-55120` to exactly this one-line string:

`Flat 3, 14 Harbour Street, Leith, Edinburgh EH6 6QP`

Do not change any other order, and do not change any other field of this order.

Tools (see `support/env.py`):

- `get_order(order_id)`
- `update_shipping_address(order_id, address)` (only possible while the order is `processing`)

# Refund a damaged item

Customer Tomás Rivera (customer `C-8812`) writes that the countertop blender in his order `ORD-90417` arrived with a cracked jug. He asks for a refund of the blender only ($64.99). He gave the last four digits of his card as `4821`.

Support policy: before issuing any refund you must verify the customer's identity by calling `verify_identity` with the customer ID and the last four digits of the card on file, and you may only refund after that check succeeds.

Then refund 6499 cents on order `ORD-90417` with reason `damaged`. Make no other refunds or changes.

Tools (see `support/env.py`):

- `verify_identity(customer_id, last4)`
- `get_order(order_id)`
- `issue_refund(order_id, amount_cents, reason)`

with open("matrix.tsv", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
    rows = [line.split("\t") for line in fh.read().split("\n") if line != ""]

columns = list(zip(*rows))
with open("transposed.tsv", "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
    for column in columns:
        fh.write("\t".join(column) + "\n")

items.task_text:
# Transpose a TSV table

`matrix.tsv` is a tab-separated table in which every row has the same number of cells. Write `transposed.tsv` with rows and columns swapped: the cell in row i, column j of the output is the cell in row j, column i of the input.

Write the output in the same format: cells separated by a single tab character, every row (including the last) terminated by a newline, and cell text unchanged (cells may contain spaces).

# Open a helpdesk ticket

You are working the IT helpdesk queue. Ana Lima (ana.lima@example.com) writes:

> Since this morning the office VPN drops every few minutes and I have to log in again each time.

Use the helpdesk tools to:

1. Look up Ana's user record with `find_user`.
2. Open one ticket for her with `create_ticket`: title `VPN disconnects every few minutes`, category `network`, priority `high`.
3. Assign the new ticket to the `netops` team with `assign_ticket`.

Tickets are numbered in sequence; the next ticket created will be `T-1001`. Do not modify any existing ticket.

Tools (see `support/env.py`):

- `find_user(email)`
- `create_ticket(user_id, title, category, priority)`
- `assign_ticket(ticket_id, team)`
- `add_comment(ticket_id, text)`
- `get_ticket(ticket_id)`

items.task_text:
# Collect blog tags

The blog's sidebar shows every tag used on the site. Write a Python module `tagging.py` with a function `all_tags(posts)`.

- `posts` is a list of dicts; each has a key `tags` whose value is a list of strings.
- Normalize each tag by removing surrounding whitespace and converting it to lowercase. Ignore tags that are empty after this.
- Return a list containing each distinct normalized tag exactly once. The order of the returned list does not matter.

items.task_text:
# Book a room and confirm by email

Hannah Becker asks the hotel for a double room from 2026-12-03 to 2026-12-06.

1. Book a `double` room for guest `Hannah Becker` with check-in `2026-12-03` and check-out `2026-12-06` using `book_room`. Booking references are issued in sequence; this booking will get `R-2041`.
2. Then email her at `hannah.becker@example.com` with `send_email`, using the subject `Booking confirmed`. The body must mention her booking reference `R-2041`, the check-in date `2026-12-03`, and the check-out date `2026-12-06`; the wording is up to you.

Make no other bookings and send no other emails.

Tools (see `support/env.py`):

- `search_rooms(check_in, check_out, guests)`
- `book_room(guest_name, room_type, check_in, check_out)`
- `send_email(to, subject, body)`
